task: Productize a user-authorized unattended cross-host scheduler for Claude Code, Gemini, and Codex without weakening Lattice authority boundaries.
outcome: User runs: lattice dispatch_policy check --policy=nightly-safe; lattice host_runtime_probe --host=claude-code --json; lattice dispatch_auto --storyId=B-xxxx --policy=nightly-safe; lattice dispatch_watch --dispatchId=D-xxxx; lattice dispatch_cancel --dispatchId=D-xxxx when needed; lattice dispatch_review --dispatchId=D-xxxx. The terminal clearly shows whether the policy authorized the run, which host workers started or were refused, how to cancel a running worker, where transcripts/receipts/diffs are, and the final manual nextAction: inspect, retry, stop, or run dispatch_merge_plan. The output never says productionDone=true, receiptVerified=true, authorityChanged=true, auto-merged, or auto-DONE.
facts: B-106b landed Lattice Host Overflow with dispatch_plan/prepare/run/collect/status/review/merge_plan and fake parallel execution.
Current real host runtimes are scaffolded only; Lattice records metadata and expects manual host execution.
host_runtime_list currently sees fake ready and claude-code/gemini/codex scaffolded with command paths available on this machine.
Claude Code CLI is installed locally as claude 2.1.143.
Gemini/Codex exact noninteractive flags and budget telemetry are treated as capability/policy degradations unless mechanically proven, not as blockers or assumed support.
The user wants to validate practical parallel development using Claude Code CLI agents while keeping host-neutral authority.
constraints: Unattended mode must be explicit opt-in through a user policy; no policy means supervised/manual fallback.
External host output cannot auto-merge, auto-DONE, verify receipts, change authority, or claim productionDone.
Policy must bound hosts, paths, denied paths, env, timeout, retry, budget/network posture, and parallelism.
Every worker must run in isolated worktree/cwd with transcript, status, cancellation, and receipt/diff review surfaces.
Implementation will use at most three concurrent Claude Code CLI development workers per wave to avoid file ownership conflicts.
Any host capability uncertainty must be rendered as unattendedSafe=false or supervised-only with nextAction.
